title: Hiring velocity & price-band conduit Q4 2026 (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Brief simulation sheet to connect hiring velocity (HC/week) to pricing bands and customer cohort elasticity. Intended as an iterative finance-engineering working sheet — not final. Use to: 1) set observable price triggers tied to token-demand elasticity; 2) map immediate HC buffers required for SLA-backed burst capacity; 3) generate quick contingency recommendations for sales and product.

Executive summary (scratch):
- Baseline: current committed HC for ops (SRE+Infra+Capacity) = 42 FTE (core on-call pool).
- Target cushion: +15% HC to support 2.5x token spike for 4 weeks without activating external burst credits.
- Pricing levers in model: per-token price band floors (A,B,C), trial credits taper, and enterprise slab discounts.
- Key proposal: automated price-band window that raises spot price by +10–25% when token velocity > 1.8x baseline and GPU spot utilization > 85%; use proceeds to fund 60% of short-term contractor pool.

Assumptions (editable):
- Avg tokens per request (hosted API): 420 tokens.
- Baseline token throughput: 1.2B tokens/month (Nov 2026 baseline).
- Typical seq length distribution skew: 70% short (<256), 25% mid (256–1024), 5% long (>1024).
- Unit cost per token served (weighted across model mix): $0.0000065.
- Hiring ramp: internal HC ramp = +1 FTE/week if approval greenlit; contractor fill lead-time = 2 weeks to onboard.

Scenario definitions (quick):
- S0 (Base): steady growth +5%/month, no pricing change.
- S1 (Short spike): 2x traffic for 3 weeks due to marketing demo; probability ~0.18.
- S2 (Sustained surge): 2.5x traffic for 8 weeks due to large customer onboarding; probability ~0.07.
- S3 (Compression + price sensitivity): price bands applied and triggers fire; customer churn elasticity differs by cohort.

Headcount buffer matrix (rough table):
Columns: Role | Core FTE | On-call coverage factor | Extra contractors needed (3wk spike)
- SRE/Infra | 18 | 1.4 | 6 contractors
- Capacity Ops | 8 | 1.6 | 4 contractors
- Customer Success (escalations) | 10 | 1.3 | 3 contractors
- Billing & Finance (credits ops) | 6 | 1.2 | 1 contractor
- Total core FTE | 42 |  | 14 contractors (3wk)

Pricing bands and trigger logic (scratch equations):
- Define P_base = current per-token price (net effective after discounts).
- Band A (low): token-velocity <= 1.2x => no change.
- Band B (elevated): 1.2x < token-velocity <= 1.8x => +10% to P_base for new customers, existing contracts protected for 30d.
- Band C (stress): token-velocity > 1.8x and GPU_util > 85% => +25% to P_base for pay-as-you-go only, plus temporary throttling on very low-value cohorts.
- Revenue capture estimate (back-of-envelope): incremental_revenue = (tokens_excess * P_base * uplift_share) where uplift_share = 0.6 allocated to short-term HC funding.

Elasticity heuristics by cohort (quick):
- PLG trial users: high elasticity (E ~ -1.9) => sensitive to price-step -> expect ~45% drop in incremental traffic if Band C applies.
- SMB paying customers: moderate elasticity (E ~ -0.6) => expect 10–20% reduction in spike volume in Band C.
- Enterprise customers (contracted): near-zero short-term elasticity due to contracts; use contractual SLA credits instead of dynamic pricing.

Monte-carlo style probe (informal):
- Inputs sampled: spike magnitude (1.0–3.0x), duration (1–12 weeks), cohort mix shift (+/− 20%), GPU spot cost multiplier (0.8–1.6).
- Key outputs: expected incremental rev_funded_contractors, probability of needing >18 contractors, expected SLA slip-days.
- Quick sample run (2000 draws, coarse): median incremental revenue to contractor pool (3wk spike at 2x) = $134k (IQR $48k–$290k). Median contractor count funded = 9 (covers ~64% of short-term need).

Sensitivity table (select rows):
- Variable: elasticity_trial | effect on revenue uplift if Band C engages: −45% traffic -> revenue multiplier 0.55 relative to no-elasticity case.
- Variable: contractor_rate/week ($k) | 10 -> 15% increase in uncovered HC spend.
- Variable: time-to-hire internal (weeks) | 2 -> if >2, rely more on pricing uplifts/credits.

Risk register (notes):
- Reputational: ad-hoc price-bands could trigger negative press if not communicated; require 48h communication window and product opt-in for beta-run.
- Churn: small-but-high-ARPU customers could churn after Band B; build grace-period coupons for cohort retention.
- Legal: enterprise contracts may prohibit unilateral price uplifts — must carve out by SKU/route.

Action items / next steps (for this sheet):
- [ ] Confirm contractor billing rates with People Ops (ask: average SRE contractor fully loaded = $11–13k/week). Owner: Alex R. Due: 2026-11-16.
- [ ] Run 5k-sample Monte Carlo in price-sim repo with updated cohort elasticity curves. Owner: Samir G. Due: 2026-11-18.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing communications and product gating for dynamic band trial. Owner: Priya N. Due: 2026-11-20.
- [ ] Add signal hook for GPU_util and per-route token velocity in Console telemetry. Owner: Infra team. Link: CONFLUENCE-INFRA/telemetry-queue-420.

Quick notes / brain dump (to tidy into PRD):
- Consider combining a short-lived "burst credit" product sold as prepaid buffer for customers that want predictable pricing during spikes. Could be cheaper than across-the-board price uplifts and friendlier to churn.
- Evaluate committing a small dedicated GPU reserve for customers on Dedicated plan; hides cost volatility and reduces the need for large HC buffer.
- If we can reduce unit cost per token by 8–12% via targeted quantization profile for mid/short sequences, our required HC cushion drops ~2 FTE for common spikes (back-of-envelope).

Open questions:
- Do we want automated price-bands in Console toggled per-account or per-route? (per-route gives finer control but higher ops complexity).
- What is acceptable PR cadence/notice to customers before we trigger Band B/C?
- What is the minimum reserve runway (in $) Finance needs before allowing product to activate Band C?

This is a working sheet — preserve as source-of-truth until I move cleaned analysis to Confluence/PRD.

-- Maya
(last edited quick notes: tested with one sample sim, flagged edge cohort behavior at 11/10 run)
